text:
alex: Heads-up — ArgoCD prune wave for the app-of-apps got aborted when reconciling infra/namespaces. Seeing 'resource not owned by application' / ownerReference mismatch errors, prune canceled. This is blocking the new GPU pool rollout to us-west-2.

maria: :eyes: can you paste the exact error? ownerReferences or labels?

alex: Exact snippet from argocd-controller log: "prune skipped: resource not owned by application (ownerReferences differ)". Namespace metadata shows label gitops-owned: infra-team but the ApplicationSet expects app.kubernetes.io/instance: appset-infra. Terraform also reports the namespace as managed by module.k8s.namespace["gpu-pool"].

sam: If TF created it originally then ArgoCD shouldn't prune it. But our appset needs to own it for the cluster bootstrap flow — so ownership drift is the problem.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] argocd/appset-sync failed for appset-infra at 2026-03-17T14:12:14Z — Prune wave cancelled (code: PRUNE_OWNER_MISMATCH) :warning:

maria: What's the impact on workloads? are GPU nodes stuck or autoscaler jobs backlogged?

alex: Nodegroup provisioning scripts expect RBAC/ServiceAccount to exist in namespace gpu-pool. Because ArgoCD skipped applying resources, pods for cloud-init and node join are failing; 3 GPU nodes are Unjoined — ~12% capacity impact in us-west-2.

sam: Quick options: 1) Add ownerReferences to the namespace pointing at the ApplicationSet (risky if TF still treats it as owner). 2) Import the namespace into TF state as a resource ArgoCD won't manage. 3) Patch labels to make ArgoCD accept it. OwnerReferences is the strict part.

maria: We should avoid state surgery during rollout. Maybe a short maintenance window to patch ownerRefs and then do a controlled TF state adopt.

alex: Draft patch I ran locally (needs UID):

kubectl annotate namespace gpu-pool argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=appset-infra --overwrite
kubectl patch namespace gpu-pool -p '{"metadata":{"ownerReferences":[{"apiVersion":"argoproj.io/v1alpha1","kind":"ApplicationSet","name":"appset-infra","uid":"<APPLICATIONSET-UID>"}]}}'

That makes ArgoCD recognize ownership and allows prune/apply to continue. Will need infra-eng approval.

sam: :+1: get infra-eng signoff. Also add a one-off ArgoCD Application arg to skip prune for that namespace in future until state is resolved (e.g., use skip: true).

ops-bot: Runbook suggestion — see https://redwood-internal/runbooks/gitops/namespace-ownership (contains recommended steps and audit checklist).

maria: I'll open a low-priority incident and loop in infra-eng and security for the UID patch. We also need to update the Terraform module to either adopt or explicitly ignore ownerReferences/labels so we don't flip-flop.

alex: Will fetch the ApplicationSet UID and post it here once I have infra approval. For now this is blocking the gpu-pool rollout in us-west-2. :frowning:

maria: Thanks — keep updates here. If we can't get approval in 4 hours we'll rollback the rollout to avoid further cluster instability.

sam: Also adding note for postmortem: consider forcing namespace creation purely via GitOps (remove TF namespace resource) or define a clear ownership handoff doc.

alex: Update — got infra-eng ack, pulling UID now. Will patch during the 15m maintenance window and monitor node joins.

maria: Nice. Post results and any logs.
